issues.where: frames 3572 to 3580, rings right of the planet
issues.what: the planet's shadow on the rings vanishes as the dive goes close, and the moon drops out in the same step. The lighting changes in one jump, not along the move. The shadow comes back just as suddenly on the way out (sheet-05.png, 3844 to 3850)
issues.fix: keep the planet-on-ring shadow on through the dive and terrain views, at every level of detail, so the shadow stays put while the camera moves

issues.what: for about 180 frames the view barely changes. The near ring bands and the planet horizon hardly move against each other, so the view reads as a held still, not a low flight with depth
issues.fix: add slow forward or sideways travel over the rings so the near bands pass clearly faster than the planet limb, and let the ring particles or bands drift in their orbit

issues.where: outer ring, lower left, frames 3596 to 3600 (also sheet-02.png 3597 to 3613)
issues.what: the motion blur on the outer ring breaks up into dark lumpy smudges and repeated band edges. It does not read as one smooth streak
issues.fix: take more motion-blur samples, or blur along the true screen-space velocity, during the fast part of the dive

issues.where: outer ring, lower left, frames 3835 to 3838
issues.what: the same blotchy, doubled blur on the outer ring comes back at the start of the rise cover
issues.fix: use the same blur sampling fix as in the dive

issues.what: the Milky Way and starfield fade quickly toward black as the camera pulls out, so the background exposure seems to shift. It also does not match the hold, where the background stays bright
issues.fix: lock exposure for the background through the rise, or ease any exposure change over a longer stretch

issues.where: fine ring bands across the frame
issues.what: the dense, thin concentric ring lines are very likely to shimmer or crawl in motion. A sampled sheet cannot rule that out
issues.fix: pre-filter or mip the ring band texture, and check a run of consecutive frames for aliasing
